title: Word Net
mascotLines: One extra paragraph in the MIT licence, and GitHub called it "Other".
Two-player mode settles who in the room reads people best.
imageCaptions: The reveal: the net drops, the reference score lands in it, and Perfect! pops up
On a phone: home with level and packs, casting the net, and the reveal
Result card: the closer your dots sit to the diagonal, the better you read the room
Two-player mode: both nets on one scale, and the round goes to the closer one
why: In 2018 it collected sentiment labels: read a sentence, drag a slider, send it to a Google Form. By 2026 its Heroku sentence server and the old Sheets API were gone, so it came back as a game with 600 original sentences. Now it labels nothing for anyone: your answers, streaks and ranks never leave the browser.
gains: A few minutes of reading what people mean rather than what they say: sarcasm, self-mockery and hidden meanings each have a pack, and every sentence has its own reply at the reveal. The two-player mode settles who in the room actually reads the room.

lessons: Appending a note to the MIT LICENSE made GitHub list it as "Other"; the note moved to the README and the sentence packs' own licence file.
Every pack must be at least 15% clearly sad and 15% clearly happy, or a single-pack game turns into a long run of "slightly negative".
The irony explanation was on screen but not in the live region, so screen-reader users heard the score without the part that trips people up.
subtitle: Catch the feeling behind a sentence
description: Read a sentence, cast a net on the sad-to-happy scale and reveal its reference score. Five modes, including daily challenges and two-player games.
longDescription: A Traditional Chinese mood-guessing game about what people mean, including sarcasm and self-deprecation. Play classic, timed, survival, daily or two-player modes, then take away a result card with your emotion map. Scores are editorial references, not psychological measurements.
features: Five game modes, including same-device two-player
Original sentences with explanations and varied feedback
Streaks, achievements and a shareable emotion-map card
